items.stem: Who was Mario, and what did he like to boast about?
items.answer: Mario was a boy who loved to boast about how many friends he had at school. He liked showing off how friendly he was with everyone.

items.stem: What challenge did Mario's grandfather present to him?
items.answer: Mario's grandfather challenged him by saying that not all of Mario's friends were real friends, and he bet a fruit chaat on it.

items.stem: Why did Mario accept his grandfather's challenge?
items.answer: Mario accepted the challenge because he was confident that he had many friends and wanted to prove his grandfather wrong.

items.stem: How did Mario's grandfather plan to help him?
items.answer: Mario's grandfather suggested using an invisible chair to test who his real friends were, saying it would reveal the truth.

items.stem: What was special about the invisible chair?
items.answer: The invisible chair was magical. If Mario could sit on it, the chair would help him figure out who his real friends were.

items.stem: Why did Mario's grandfather doubt that Mario had many true friends?
items.answer: Mario's grandfather doubted that Mario had many true friends because he believed most of Mario's so-called friends were just companions or partners, not true friends. He wanted Mario to understand the difference between real friends and people who only pretend to be friends.

items.stem: How did Mario feel about the invisible chair when he first saw it?
items.answer: When Mario first saw the invisible chair, he couldn't actually see it and found the idea confusing. However, he trusted his grandfather and agreed to take the invisible chair to school, hoping it would help him discover who his real friends were.

items.stem: What was Mario unsure about after accepting the challenge?
items.answer: After accepting the challenge, Mario was unsure how he could test whether his schoolmates were real friends or just companions. He didn't know how to prove the difference between true friends and others.

items.stem: How did Mario's grandfather describe the invisible chair?
items.answer: Mario's grandfather described the invisible chair as something magical but tricky to sit on. He said that if Mario managed to sit on it, the magic would reveal his true friends.

items.stem: What did Mario's grandfather mean when he said some of Mario's friends were "nothing more than companions or partners"?
items.answer: Mario's grandfather meant that many of Mario's friends were not genuine friends. They might be people he spent time with or worked with, but they didn't share the bond of true friendship.

items.stem: Why did Mario's grandfather decide to give him the invisible chair?
items.answer: Mario's grandfather gave him the invisible chair because he wanted Mario to learn the difference between real friends and those who were just companions. The grandfather understood that Mario was proud of the number of friends he had, but he suspected that not all of them were true friends. By giving Mario the invisible chair, he provided him with a way to test the loyalty and sincerity of his friends, hoping Mario would realise that the quality of friends matters more than quantity.

items.stem: What was the significance of the invisible chair in the story?
items.answer: The invisible chair symbolised the way in which true friendships are revealed in difficult or challenging situations. It was a magical test for Mario to discover which of his friends were genuinely supportive. Just as sitting on the chair required trust and patience, real friends stand by you when things get tricky or when you're most vulnerable, showing that they care deeply and sincerely.

items.stem: How does the invisible chair serve as a test of friendship?
items.answer: The invisible chair serves as a test of friendship by revealing who Mario's true friends are. Only the friends who are willing to believe in something invisible or unusual, like the magic chair, and support Mario in his efforts are considered true friends. It shows that real friends believe in you even when things seem impossible, while others may doubt or leave you behind.

items.stem: What lesson did Mario's grandfather want him to learn from this experience?
items.answer: Mario's grandfather wanted him to learn that friendship is about quality, not quantity. He wanted Mario to realise that many people may seem like friends, but only a few will stand by you in challenging or uncertain situations. By giving Mario the invisible chair, he hoped that Mario would understand the difference between true friends who care about you and casual companions who may only be around for fun.

items.stem: How does the idea of an invisible chair relate to trust and belief in friendships?
items.answer: The invisible chair symbolises trust and belief in friendships because real friends are those who support you even when they can't see or fully understand your struggles. Like sitting on an invisible chair, friendships require faith in each other. True friends trust you even in confusing or difficult circumstances, whereas others may doubt you when things become unclear or complicated.

items.stem: How do you think Mario's view of friendship will change after using the invisible chair?
items.answer: Mario's view of friendship is likely to change as he realises that not all his friends are true friends. He may come to value the few friends who genuinely care for him over the many casual friends who are only around for fun.

items.stem: How does the grandfather's approach help Mario learn an important life lesson?
items.answer: The grandfather's approach is hands-on and creative. By using the invisible chair, he teaches Mario through experience rather than just words. This approach helps Mario truly understand the difference between real and fake friends, making the lesson more impactful.

items.stem: What role does the invisible chair play in revealing the true nature of friendships?
items.answer: The invisible chair plays the role of a test that exposes the sincerity of Mario's friendships. Friends who are willing to believe in the chair and support Mario show themselves as loyal and trustworthy, while those who doubt or laugh at the idea are not real friends.

items.stem: Why is it important to distinguish between true friends and casual companions?
items.answer: It is important to distinguish between true friends and casual companions because true friends offer emotional support, loyalty, and trust, especially in difficult times. Casual companions might only be around for fun and could leave when faced with challenges, offering little real friendship.

items.stem: How does this story teach about the value of trust in friendships?
items.answer: The story teaches that trust is a key part of friendship. True friends are willing to believe in you and your struggles, even when things are not visible or easy to understand, just as Mario's true friends will trust him with the invisible chair.

items.stem: Why do you think Mario was so eager to prove his grandfather wrong?
items.answer: Mario was eager to prove his grandfather wrong because he took pride in having many friends and didn't want to admit that some of them might not be true friends.

items.stem: What might have happened if Mario had not asked for his grandfather's help?
items.answer: Without his grandfather's help, Mario might not have realised that not all his friends were genuine. He could have continued believing that the quantity of friends mattered more than the quality of his friendships.

items.stem: How do you think Mario will feel after discovering who his real friends are?
items.answer: Mario might feel surprised or even disappointed after discovering that some of his friends are not true friends. However, he will likely appreciate and value the few real friends who stand by him.

items.stem: What does the story suggest about the nature of friendships in challenging situations?
items.answer: The story suggests that friendships are tested in challenging situations. True friends will support and believe in you when things are difficult, while casual companions may not be there when you need them most.

items.stem: How does the story's message relate to real-life friendships?
items.answer: The story's message relates to real life by showing that not everyone you call a friend is a true friend. True friendships are built on trust, support, and loyalty, and they often become clear in times of difficulty or need.
